etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From French similarité.

Morphologically similar +‎ -ity

definitions.definition: Closeness of appearance to something else.

quote.citation: 1859–1860, William Hamilton, edited by H[enry] L[ongueville] Mansel and John Veitch, Lectures on Metaphysics and Logic […], volume (please specify |volume=I to IV), Edinburgh, London: William Blackwood and Sons, →OCLC:
quote.text: Hardly is there a similarity detected between two or three facts, than men hasten to extend it to all.

definitions.definition: (geometry) A transformation (of a Euclidean space) that preserves angles and the ratios of distances
(mathematics, linear algebra) The property of two matrices being similar.
